Charles Booker

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, Kentucky · Open seat

Former Kentucky state representative; U.S. Senate candidate

Charles Booker is a Louisville Democrat who served one term in the Kentucky House of Representatives. He ran for U.S. Senate in 2020 (he lost the Democratic primary) and in 2022 (he lost the general election). He entered the 2026 race for the seat Mitch McConnell is leaving in December 2025 and won the Democratic primary in May 2026.

Where Booker stands

Wages and cost of living
Proposes a '40x40x45' plan: anyone working 40 hours a week would be guaranteed at least 40 hours of paid sick leave and at least $45,000 a year in pay. He would also back a Cost of Living Tax Exemption to make that $45,000 tax-free.
Taxes
Supports a wealth tax and taxing capital gains at the same rates as wages. Proposes closing loopholes that he says let corporations and billionaires pay lower taxes than workers.
Health care
Supports Medicare for All. Says health care is a human right.
Affordability
Says his 'Kentucky First' agenda would lower prices by investing in Kentuckians and supporting small businesses. Blames Barr for rising grocery and gas prices.
Foreign policy / Iran
Says the U.S. should 'end endless war' and bring service members home. Tied Barr to President Trump on the Iran war.
Data centers
Called for a moratorium on data centers during the Senate debate.
Surveillance / Flock cameras
Supports limits on Flock license-plate cameras. Says the country must 'stand against the use of mass surveillance.'
Term limits
Supports a limit of two terms for U.S. senators.
Poverty and public safety
Names affordability and public safety as key issues and says his broader goal is ending generational poverty.
